title: [YouPass Collect] - Australian secondary school leavers' employment and education trends

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the percentages of Australian school leavers who secured employment, remained unemployed, or enrolled in further education in 1980, 1990, and 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the proportion of school leavers entering the workforce increased steadily over the period, whereas those continuing their studies experienced a decline. In contrast, unemployment rates fluctuated throughout. Additionally, by the final year, employment had overtaken further education as the predominant outcome.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the two primary outcomes, in 1980, further education was chosen by half of all school leavers, 10 percentage points higher than employment, which stood at 40%. Over the next two decades, the employment figure rose progressively, reaching 50% in 1990 and peaking at 55% by 2000. Meanwhile, the proportion pursuing further education fell considerably, dropping to 38% in 1990 before declining further to 37% in the final year.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Turning to unemployment, it accounted for just 10% of school leavers in 1980, making it the smallest category. This figure increased to peak at 12% in 1990, before falling back to 8% by 2000.
